mxCell.value: QCAU DETAILED DATAFLOW - READ THIS PAGE FIRST
Current code reference: inference/QCAU.py + inference/model.py | Shapes below use inference/config.json defaults and show MP=1 plus MP=4 local examples.

SYMBOLS AND DEFAULT NUMBERS
B = batch size; default max_batch_size = 4 S = query sequence length; 1 for decode; up to 4096 D = model hidden width = 4096 H = query heads = 64 H_local = H / world_size = 64 (MP=1), 16 (MP=4) Dh = attention head width = 512 R = rope_head_dim = 64; non-RoPE width = 448 G = output groups = 8; G_local = 8 (MP=1), 2 (MP=4) OR = output low-rank width = 1024 W = sliding window = 128 K_index = 512 for learned indexer T = QCAU tile_size = 64 eps = 1e-6; scale = 1/sqrt(Dh) = 0.04419417

INPUT FROM TRANSFORMER BLOCK
x: [B,S,D] = [B,S,4096] For model path, x arrives after Block.attn_norm.
Weights and state: wq_a [1024,4096] wq_b [32768,1024] = [H*Dh,q_rank] wkv [512,4096] q_norm_weight [1024] kv_norm_weight [512] freqs_cis [max_seq_len,R/2] = [4096,32] complex attn_sink [H_local] topk_idxs [B,S,K_total] KV cache [B,N,512]

A. Q PREPROCESSING
QCAU.py full mode: 1. q_low = x @ wq_a.T 2. q_low = RMSNorm(q_low) 3. q_flat = q_low @ wq_b.T 4. reshape [B,S,H_local,Dh] 5. per-head RMS-like normalization 6. RoPE on last R=64 dimensions
Output q: [B,S,H_local,512]
Model path performs the same operations in Attention.forward() before calling QCAU core.

B. KV PREPROCESSING / CACHE / ADDRESS
1. kv_current = x @ wkv.T 2. KV RMSNorm 3. RoPE on last R=64 dimensions 4. Write sliding-window cache 5. Optional Compressor writes compressed rows 6. Window or learned Indexer creates addresses
QCAU input kv: [B,N,512] topk_idxs: [B,S,K_total] with -1 invalid entries
Compressor and Indexer live in model.py; QCAU.py has deterministic helper paths when topk is omitted.

C. QCAU SPARSE ATTENTION CORE
For tile_base = 0, T, 2T, ...: 1. read topk index tile [B,S,T] 2. valid = 0 <= idx < N 3. clamp invalid indices for safe gather 4. gather KV tile [B,S,T,Dh] 5. QK dot product [B,S,H_local,T] 6. scale by 1/sqrt(Dh) 7. masked online softmax 8. weighted V accumulation
State per [B,S,H_local]: scores_max, sum_exp State per [B,S,H_local,Dh]: acc_o

D. OUTPUT RESTORATION
1. Add attention sink to denominator only 2. o = acc_o / final_sum_exp 3. inverse RoPE on output tail [R=64] 4. reshape into G_local output groups 5. wo_a: group width 4096 -> OR=1024 6. flatten groups 7. wo_b: [G*OR] -> D=4096
QCAU standalone output: [B,S,D] when wo_a/wo_b are supplied. Attention.forward() returns x: [B,S,4096] to the transformer block.

OUTPUT DESTINATION
attention output x: [B,S,D] = [B,S,4096]
In model.py this is returned from Attention.forward(), then passed to Hyper-Connections in Block.forward(). The QCAU core itself returns [B,S,H_local,Dh] before inverse RoPE and wo projection.

IMPORTANT CODE BOUNDARY
QCAU.py: self-contained PyTorch reference. It contains projections, cache helper, address helper, sparse core and optional output projection.
model.py Attention.forward(): actual model integration. It computes Q/KV, Compressor, Indexer, cache and topk_idxs, then calls QCAU(q, kv, attn_sink, topk_idxs).
kernel.py: TileLang GPU implementation of sparse_attn. It is not the primary RTL golden model in this document.
x [B,S,4096] + weights
q [B,S,H_local,512]
kv [B,N,512] + topk_idxs [B,S,K_total]
o [B,S,H_local,512]
x_out [B,S,4096]
QCAU.py EXACT FUNCTIONAL PATH
This page follows the current QCAU(c_q, w_uq, kv, topk_idxs, attn_sink, freqs_cis) interface. ACU, LIU and GOPU are outside this page.

QCAU INPUT CONTRACT
c_Q: [B,S,D_C] Latent query from Query Down / LIU.
kv: [B,N,Dh] KV rows already prepared by ACU and selected/addressed by LIU.
topk_idxs: [B,S,K] Addresses into kv; invalid entries are -1.
attn_sink: [H_local] freqs_cis: full RoPE table or [S,R/2] slice start_pos selects positions when a full table is supplied.

1. QUERY UP
w_uq may be a tensor or callable projector.
2D weight: q_flat = c_Q @ W_UQ.T
3D weight forms accepted: [D_C,H,Dh] or [H,D_C,Dh]
Output: [B,S,H_local*Dh] or [B,S,H_local,Dh]

2. HEAD RESHAPE + RMSNORM
q = unflatten(q_flat, [H_local,Dh])
For the Flash configuration: Dh = 512 H_local = 64 (MP=1) or 16 (MP=4)
q[h] = q[h] / sqrt(mean(q[h]^2) + eps) Optional q_head_norm_weight[H_local,Dh] is applied per head.
Output q: [B,S,H_local,512]

3. QUERY RoPE (+position)
Rotate only the final rope_head_dim values. Default rope_head_dim = 64, giving 32 complex pairs.
q_tail_rot = q_tail * freqs_cis[position]
The first Dh - 64 values are unchanged. If freqs_cis is full, use rows start_pos:start_pos+S.
Output q_rot: [B,S,H_local,512]

4. CORE MQA + ONLINE SOFTMAX
For tile_base = 0, T, 2T, ...: 1. Read topk_idxs tile [B,S,T]. 2. valid = (idx >= 0) & (idx < N). 3. Clamp only for safe KV gather. 4. Gather kv_tile [B,S,T,Dh]. 5. QK dot product [B,S,H_local,T]. 6. Scale by 1/sqrt(Dh). 7. Update running max, denominator and weighted-V state.
The same KV row is broadcast to every query head (MQA). State is kept in FP32 in the reference.

5. ATTENTION SINK + OUTPUT
After all KV tiles: sink_term = exp(attn_sink - scores_max) sink contributes to denominator only.
o_core = acc_o / final_denominator
Output before inverse RoPE: [B,S,H_local,Dh]
All-invalid addresses remain finite and produce zero value output when the sink is finite.

6. OUTPUT RoPE (-position)
Apply the conjugate frequency to the final rope_head_dim values.
o[..., -64:] = o_core[..., -64:] * freqs_cis[position].conj()
The prefix remains unchanged.
QCAU return value: o [B,S,H_local,Dh]
This is the interface to GOPU. QCAU does not perform wo_a, wo_b or all-reduce.

OUTSIDE QCAU
ACU: creates and stores KV rows. LIU: creates c_Q, scores compressed candidates and supplies topk_idxs. GOPU: receives o and performs grouped output projection.
QCAU.py does not receive x, does not build KV/cache/indexes and does not project o back to model width.
c_Q + W_UQ
q normalized
q_rot + kv + topk_idxs + sink
online attention output
QCAU CORE: ONE ONLINE-ATTENTION TILE
Exact logical operations from _sparse_attention_online(). T is normally 64. The loop repeats for tile_base = 0,64,128,... until K_total is consumed.

Q INPUT
q [B,S,H,Dh] default [B,S,64,512] MP=1 local [B,S,16,512] MP=4
q_float = q.float() Compute dtype: FP32 in reference

INDEX TILE
idxs = topk_idxs[..., tile_base:tile_base+T]
topk_idxs [B,S,K_total] tile_idxs [B,S,T] T=64 except final partial tile
Convert to torch.long on q device.

VALIDITY CHECK
valid = (tile_idxs >= 0) & (tile_idxs < N)
Shape: [B,S,T] True means this address contributes. False means invalid/future/out-of-range.

SAFE ADDRESS CLAMP
safe_idxs = clamp(tile_idxs, 0, max(N-1,0))
Shape: [B,S,T]
Purpose: make gather memory-safe even for -1 or an out-of-range index. The valid mask later removes its numerical contribution.

GATHER INDEX EXPAND
gather_index = safe_idxs.unsqueeze(-1).expand(B,S,T,Dh)
Shape: [B,S,T,512] The same row address is replicated across all Dh=512 value lanes.

KV TILE GATHER
kv_float [B,N,512] torch.gather along dimension 1 using gather_index
Initial gather result reshaped: [B,S*T,512] -> [B,S,T,512]
kv_tile = where(valid[...,None], kv_tile, 0) Invalid rows become zero vectors.

QK DOT PRODUCT
scores = einsum bshd,bstd->bsht(q_float, kv_tile)
Input q: [B,S,H,512] Input kv_tile: [B,S,T,512] Output scores: [B,S,H,T]
For every b,s,h,t: dot = sum d=0..511 q[b,s,h,d] * kv_tile[b,s,t,d]

SCALE + MASK
scores *= softmax_scale default softmax_scale = Dh^(-1/2) for Dh=512: 0.0441941738
scores = where(valid.unsqueeze(2), scores, -inf)
Output masked scores: [B,S,H,T]

RUNNING STATE BEFORE TILE
scores_max_prev [B,S,H] = -inf initially sum_exp [B,S,H] = 0 initially acc_o [B,S,H,512] = 0 initially
All three are FP32 in QCAU.py. They persist across tile iterations for the same batch/query/head.

TILE REDUCTION OUTPUTS
tile_has_valid = any(valid,-1) tile_max = amax(scores,-1) [B,S,H] next_scores_max = maximum(prev,tile_max)
If tile has no valid index, keep previous max and use old_scale=1. This prevents -inf - -inf NaN.

TO ONLINE SOFTMAX STAGE
masked scores [B,S,H,T] valid [B,S,T] tile_max [B,S,H] previous state [m,l,o]
The next page expands the exact recurrence and weighted-V update.

RTL interpretation
T=64 rows per tile. Each row is Dh=512 values. QK engine can use 512 MAC lanes, time-multiplexed MACs, or a systolic reduction. The Python operation is a logical contract; it does not prescribe the physical PE count.

ONLINE SOFTMAX, ATTENTION SINK AND WEIGHTED-V ACCUMULATION
The algorithm never creates a [B,S,H,K_total] attention matrix in memory. It streams one tile and maintains running state.

INITIAL STATE BEFORE TILE LOOP
m_0 = scores_max = -inf Shape [B,S,H]
l_0 = sum_exp = 0 Shape [B,S,H]
o_0 = acc_o = zero Shape [B,S,H,Dh] = [B,S,H,512]
All state tensors are FP32.

1. TILE MAXIMUM AND NEW MAX
tile_has_valid = any(valid, dim=-1) Shape [B,S,1]
tile_max = amax(scores, dim=-1) Shape [B,S,H]
m_new_candidate = maximum(m_old,tile_max)
m_new = where(tile_has_valid, candidate, m_old)
For all-invalid tile, m does not change.

2. OLD MASS RESCALE
old_scale = exp(m_old - m_new) Shape [B,S,H]
If tile_has_valid=False: old_scale=1.
This converts old accumulators from the old exponent origin to the new exponent origin before adding this tile.

3. TILE EXPONENTIAL WEIGHTS
safe_m = where(isfinite(m_new),m_new,0) p = exp(scores - safe_m[...,None]) p = where(valid[...,None],p,0)
p shape [B,S,H,T] Invalid scores are exactly zero probability. When the first valid tile arrives after invalid tiles, safe_m avoids -inf - -inf.

4. NORMALIZATION MASS UPDATE
l_new = l_old * old_scale + sum(p, dim=-1)
l_old, l_new shape [B,S,H] sum(p,-1) shape [B,S,H]
This is the denominator contribution from real KV entries only. Sink is added after the tile loop.

5. WEIGHTED-V UPDATE
o_new = o_old * old_scale + einsum(p,kv_tile)
p [B,S,H,T] kv_tile [B,S,T,Dh] output o [B,S,H,Dh] = [B,S,H,512]
For each output lane d: sum over t=0..T-1 p[b,s,h,t] * kv_tile[b,s,t,d]

TILE LOOP CONTROL
tile_base = 0,64,128,...,K_total-1 tile_idxs = idxs[...,tile_base:tile_base+64]
The state [m,l,o] from this row becomes the state input to the next tile. For K_total=128, two tiles. For K_total=512, eight tiles. For K_total=640, ten tiles.

6. ATTENTION SINK AFTER ALL KV TILES
sink = attn_sink.view(1,1,H) Shape [1,1,H]
If m is finite: sink_term = exp(sink - m) If m=-inf and sink finite: sink_term = 1 If m=-inf and sink=-inf: sink_term = 0
Sink contributes to denominator only; it has no V vector.

7. FINAL NORMALIZATION
l_final = l_after_tiles + sink_term Shape [B,S,H]
den = clamp_min(l_final, tiny_FP32)
The clamp protects the divide from zero when every address is invalid and sink is -inf.

8. CORE OUTPUT
out = acc_o / den.unsqueeze(-1)
acc_o [B,S,H,Dh] den [B,S,H] broadcast den to [B,S,H,1]
Return cast to q.dtype. Output: [B,S,H_local,512]
All-invalid row with finite sink: acc_o=0, den=1, output=0. All-invalid row with sink=-inf: acc_o=0, den=tiny, output=0.

NUMERICAL CONTRACT
The reference accumulates m, l and o in FP32. It avoids materializing probability matrices beyond one tile. The exact RTL implementation may approximate exp, reciprocal and reduction, but must preserve this logical recurrence and valid-mask behavior.

m_old,m_new [B,S,H]
p [B,S,H,T]
p + kv_tile + old_scale

OUTPUT SIDE: INVERSE RoPE, GROUPED wo_a AND wo_b
The core output is still per query head. This page shows how it becomes the model hidden width D=4096.

QCAU CORE OUTPUT
o_core [B,S,H_local,Dh] MP=1: [B,S,64,512] MP=4: [B,S,16,512]
dtype returned by QCAU is q.dtype; running attention state was FP32.

INVERSE RoPE
Apply conjugate frequency to last R=64 values of each head.
Tail [B,S,H_local,64] -> 32 complex values/head. prefix [B,S,H_local,448] copied unchanged.
o_derot [B,S,H_local,512]

GROUP VIEW / HEAD CONCATENATION
o_grouped = o.view(B,S,G_local,-1)
Group width = H_local*Dh/G_local. MP=1: 64*512/8 = 4096. MP=4: 16*512/2 = 4096.
Output shape: MP=1 [B,S,8,4096] MP=4 [B,S,2,4096]

wo_a GROUPED LOW-RANK PROJECTION
Global logical weight: [G*OR, H*Dh/G] = [8192,4096].
Model local view: [G_local,OR,4096] MP=1: [8,1024,4096] MP=4: [2,1024,4096].
einsum bsgd,grd->bsgr [B,S,G_local,4096] x [G_local,1024,4096] -> [B,S,G_local,1024]

GROUP FLATTEN
o_lowrank.flatten(2)
MP=1: [B,S,8,1024] -> [B,S,8192] MP=4: [B,S,2,1024] -> [B,S,2048] local
The local MP=4 result is the input shard for RowParallelLinear wo_b.

wo_b ROW-PARALLEL LINEAR
Global logical weight [D,G*OR] = [4096,8192].
MP=1: input [B,S,8192] -> output [B,S,4096]. MP=4: local weight [4096,2048], local output [B,S,4096], then all_reduce across 4 ranks.
This restores model hidden width D=4096.

OUTPUT TO BLOCK
x_attn [B,S,D] = [B,S,4096]
In Attention.forward(): returned to Block.forward(). Block then performs hc_pre, ffn_norm, MoE, hc_post and residual mixing.

SHAPE INVARIANT
H_local * Dh = G_local * (H_local*Dh/G_local)
MP=1: 64*512 = 8*4096 = 32768. MP=4: 16*512 = 2*4096 = 8192 local.
This invariant is required for the reshape before wo_a. For standalone QCAU on MP=4, pass n_local_groups=2 (or n_groups=2) explicitly; model.py already uses self.n_local_groups.

PREFILL VS DECODE: DATAFLOW OVER TIME
The QCAU core is the same; S, cache writes, legal addresses and compressed-state updates change between prefill and decode.

PREFILL PHASE
Call: model(input_ids[:, :S], start_pos=0)
1. Input x [B,S,4096]. 2. Produce q [B,S,H_local,512]. 3. Produce kv_current [B,S,512]. 4. Fill window cache for current tokens. 5. If compression: compressor may emit S_c compressed rows. 6. Build topk_idxs per query row. 7. QCAU loops over S queries and K_total addresses. 8. Output o [B,S,H_local,512]. 9. Output projection returns [B,S,4096].
For logits, Transformer.head consumes the last sequence row later.

PREFILL CACHE STATE AFTER CALL
Window cache: [B,W,512] valid rows depend on S. Compressed cache if active: [B,N_c,512] rows at logical offset W.
For ratio=4 and S=8: current rows [B,8,512] compressed rows approximately [B,2,512] prefill QCAU kv can be [B,10,512] decode cache layout remains [B,1152,512].

DECODE PHASE, ONE TOKEN
Call: model(input_ids[:,p:p+1], start_pos=p)
1. Input x [B,1,4096]. 2. Produce q [B,1,H_local,512]. 3. Produce kv_current [B,1,512]. 4. Write window slot p % 128. 5. If compression active, update incremental compressor state. 6. If (p+1) % ratio == 0, emit compressed row. 7. Build topk_idxs [B,1,K_total]. 8. QCAU processes one query row. 9. Output projection returns [B,1,4096].
The next decode step reuses the updated cache and state.

DECODE ADDRESS EXAMPLE, W=128
p=0: valid window addresses 0; rest -1. p=1: valid addresses 0,1; rest -1. p=127: addresses 0..127. p=128: circular address order starts at 1 and wraps through 0.
For compressed ratio=4: compressed physical addresses begin at 128. Indexer selected j becomes address 128+j.
All invalid addresses remain in the packet with valid=False.

SAME QCAU CORE CONTRACT IN BOTH MODES
q [B,S,H_local,512] kv [B,N,512] topk_idxs [B,S,K_total] sink [H_local]
For each query row and tile: safe gather -> QK score -> scale/mask -> online m,l,o update -> sink -> normalize.
The only difference is how q, kv and topk_idxs are prepared and how cache state is updated.

STATE THAT PERSISTS BETWEEN DECODE CALLS
Attention.kv_cache [B,N_cache,512]. Compressor.kv_state and score_state for unfinished groups. Indexer compressed KV cache [B,N_c,128] when ratio=4. Transformer position p supplied by generate.py.
QCAU running state m,l,o does not persist across calls; it is reinitialized for each query row.

OUTPUT TO GENERATION
Attention output after wo_b: prefill [B,S,4096] decode [B,1,4096]
Transformer head selects x[:, -1] and produces logits [B,vocab_size]. generate.py samples/argmaxes the next token and invokes the next decode position.

IMPORTANT LIMIT
QCAU.py itself does not own the learned Compressor or Indexer state. Those modules live in model.py and feed QCAU. The QCAU standalone helper can create deterministic window/compressed indices if topk_idxs is omitted, but this is not the learned ratio=4 Indexer path.

REFERENCE DATA TYPES
QCAU receives q and kv in model activation dtype, normally BF16 in the working fallback path.
_sparse_attention_online immediately creates q_float and kv_float in FP32.
acc_o, sum_exp and scores_max are FP32.
Output is cast back to q.dtype.
The native TileLang kernel declares BF16 q/kv/output and FP32 attention state. An RTL design may choose BF16, FP16 or fixed point, but must document rounding and saturation.

RTL BLOCKS TO DRAW
1. Input/token stream and start_pos control 2. Q low-rank GEMM 4096x1024 3. Q expansion GEMM 1024x32768 4. Q RMS / per-head norm 5. Q RoPE complex pair rotator 6. KV GEMM 4096x512 7. KV RMS / KV RoPE 8. Window/compressed KV SRAM controller 9. Address SRAM and valid-mask generator 10. KV gather/burst buffer, T x 512 11. QK MAC/reduction engine, H x T scores 12. scale, -inf mask and exp approximation 13. running max and rescale FSM 14. weighted-V MAC and FP32 accumulator 15. sink denominator injection 16. reciprocal / output normalization 17. inverse RoPE 18. grouped wo_a GEMM/einsum 19. wo_b row-parallel GEMM/all-reduce

MUST-HOLD INVARIANTS
1. q.size(-1) == kv.size(-1) == Dh. 2. q.shape[1] == topk_idxs.shape[1]. 3. batch dimensions agree. 4. attn_sink has H_local values. 5. invalid addresses never contribute to score, sum or weighted V. 6. all-invalid tile is a no-op. 7. all-invalid row produces finite zero output. 8. group reshape preserves H_local*Dh. 9. wo_a group width is H_local*Dh/G_local. 10. decode cache write uses start_pos % W. 11. ratio=4 compressed addresses use offset W in decode. 12. inverse RoPE uses conjugate coefficient.

VERIFICATION CHECKLIST COMPLETED FOR THE REFERENCE
Core vs torch.softmax reference: max abs error about 2.4e-7. Tile sizes 1,4,64: equivalent within numerical tolerance. Invalid -1 and out-of-range indices: masked and finite. Entirely invalid tile: no NaN. Full QCAU path with projections/RoPE/wo_a/wo_b: finite and correct shape. CPU model prefill/decode: pass. GPU model prefill/decode: pass. Compressed ratio=4 GPU path: pass.
This establishes a functional golden model, not cycle-accurate RTL.

CODE TO RTL TRACEABILITY
QCAU.py:8-59 local linear/RMS/RoPE helpers QCAU.py:106-189 online sparse attention core QCAU.py:192-370 standalone orchestration and output projection model.py Attention.forward(): actual model-side Q/KV/cache/topk preparation model.py Compressor: compressed KV creation and decode state model.py Indexer: learned compressed address selection kernel.py sparse_attn: native TileLang analogue of the core
When drawing hardware, use QCAU.py recurrence as the functional contract and model.py as the producer/consumer contract.

ADDRESS / MEMORY SIZING EXAMPLES
Window-only KV SRAM: 128 rows x 512 values. Compressed ratio=4 cache: (128+1024)=1152 rows x 512 values. At 16-bit values: 1152*512*16 = 9,437,184 bits = 1,179,648 bytes per batch element per layer, before metadata.
Index tile metadata: T=64 integer addresses per query row. QK score tile: H_local x T values per query row. Weighted V accumulator: H_local x 512 values per query row.

DO NOT CONFUSE THESE THREE LEVELS
Level 1: QCAU.py = readable functional PyTorch golden model. Level 2: model.py = complete MLA integration including Compressor and Indexer. Level 3: kernel.py = TileLang GPU implementation; it describes a possible high-performance schedule, not the complete model-side address producer.
MODEL-SIDE PRODUCERS OF QCAU KV ROWS AND ADDRESSES
Compressor and Indexer are in model.py. They do not replace the QCAU core; they create compressed KV rows and top-k addresses that QCAU consumes.

ATTENTION INPUT
x [B,S,D] = [B,S,4096] qr [B,S,q_lora_rank] = [B,S,1024]
Both branches receive the same token hidden states. qr is the low-rank Q state before the main q expansion.

COMPRESSOR CANDIDATE LINEARS
Compressor.forward() converts x to float.
wkv(x): [B,S,coff*Dh] wgate(x): [B,S,coff*Dh]
coff = 1 for ratio != 4. coff = 2 for ratio=4 overlap mode. For ratio=4: width = 2*512 = 1024.

GATED RATIO POOLING, PREFILL
score = wgate(x) + ape ape [ratio,coff*Dh]
Reshape full groups: kv [B,S/r,r,coff*Dh] score [B,S/r,r,coff*Dh]

COMPRESSED KV POSTPROCESS
kv_compressed [B,S_c,512] RMSNorm over 512. RoPE on last R=64.
rotate=False: act_quant on first 448 values, block size 64. rotate=True for Indexer compressor: Hadamard rotation, then FP4 activation simulation.
Output is written into compressed cache at offset W in decode layout.

DECODE COMPRESSOR STATE
kv_state and score_state hold unfinished ratio groups.
At start_pos=p, S=1: should_compress = ((p+1) % ratio == 0)
ratio=4 overlap state has two windows: previous overlap rows and current rows. When should_compress=True, concatenate valid halves, softmax over state positions, produce one [B,1,512] row, shift state for the next group.

INDEXER QUERY PATH, ratio=4
qr [B,S,1024] wq_b_index: [H_i*D_i,1024] H_i=64 global, D_i=128 H_i_local=64/world_size
Logical q_index [B,S,64,128]. MP=4 local q_index [B,S,16,128]. Apply RoPE to last R=64. Hadamard rotation across 128. FP4 activation simulation.

INDEXER COMPRESSED KV
Indexer owns a Compressor(..., head_dim=128, rotate=True).
indexer.kv_cache [B,max_seq_len/4,128] For max_seq_len=4096: [B,1024,128].
The index compressor creates rows used only for address scoring; the main QCAU value path uses the main Attention compressed KV cache with width 512.

INDEX SCORE COMPUTE
weights = weights_proj(x) weights [B,S,H_i] scale = D_i^(-1/2) * H_i^(-1/2)
index_score = einsum(q_index, indexer.kv_cache) raw [B,S,H_i,N_c] relu(raw), multiply weights, sum over H_i
final index_score [B,S,N_c]

INDEXER MASK + TOPK
Prefill causal mask: compressed index j is invalid when j >= floor((s+1)/ratio). Invalid score becomes -inf.
topk_idxs = topk(index_score, min(index_topk,end_pos/ratio)) index_topk=512.
Prefill: selected future entries -> -1; legal entries + offset=S. Decode: selected entries + offset=W.
Output compressed_idx [B,S,K_c]

WINDOW INDEX + CONCATENATION
window_idx = get_window_topk_idxs(128,B,S,start_pos) shape [B,S,128]
If ratio=0: topk_idxs = window_idx. If ratio!=0: topk_idxs = cat(window_idx, compressed_idx). shape [B,S,128+K_c].
topk_idxs is converted to int32 and sent to QCAU with kv and q.

SEPARATION OF VALUE AND INDEX PATHS
Main Attention compressor: width 512, feeds QCAU values and latent K rows. Indexer compressor: width 128, feeds learned address scoring only.
Both paths use the same token input and position frequencies, but their output caches have different widths and must not be connected interchangeably.

KV ADDRESS PACKET, MEMORY LAYOUT AND GATHER CONTRACT
This page translates the Python dense gather into the logical SRAM interfaces an RTL QCAU would need.

ADDRESS PACKET PER QUERY ROW
topk_idxs[b,s,:] shape [K_total] int32
Pure window: K_total=128. Learned compressed layer: K_total=128+K_c.
For every local head h, the same token address list is reused with q[b,s,h,:]. There is no separate index tensor per query head in QCAU core.

TILE SELECTOR
tile_base = 0,64,128,... tile_idxs = topk_idxs[...,tile_base:tile_base+64]
Shape [B,S,T], T=64 except final tile.
One control counter selects the same tile range for all batches and query rows; tensorized Python code expresses the complete batch operation.

VALID + SAFE ADDRESS
valid = (idx >= 0) & (idx < N) safe_idx = clamp(idx,0,N-1)
valid travels with each address. safe_idx is used only to avoid illegal SRAM reads. Invalid safe reads are zeroed immediately after gather and scores are later masked to -inf.

ROW-WIDTH ADDRESS EXPANSION
gather_index = safe_idx.unsqueeze(-1).expand([B,S,T,Dh])
Dh=512. Logical index traffic is [B,S,T] addresses; the expanded index is a vectorized view used to gather all 512 row elements.

KV SRAM / CACHE VIEW
Logical tensor kv_float [B,N,512].
Window-only: N=128 rows. Ratio=4 decode cache: N=128+1024=1152 rows. Ratio=128 decode cache: N=128+32=160 rows.
Each row is 512 activation values. For 16-bit values, one ratio=4 cache is 1152*512*16 = 9,437,184 bits per batch element per layer.

GATHER RESULT
torch.gather(kv_float, dim=1, index=gather_index.reshape(B,S*T,Dh))
Intermediate: [B,S*T,512]. Reshape: [B,S,T,512]. where(valid[...,None], value, zero).
This is the exact KV tile consumed by QK and weighted-V paths.

Q ROW BUFFER
q_float[b,s,:,:] shape [H_local,512]
MP=1: [64,512]. MP=4: [16,512].
For one query row, this buffer is reused for all T tiles. The KV tile changes each iteration.

SCORE TILE BUFFER
scores [H_local,T] per query row
MP=1: [64,64] values. MP=4: [16,64] values.
After scale and valid mask, this tile feeds max reduction, exp and weighted-V accumulation.

PER-QUERY RUNNING STATE
For one b,s: m [H_local] l [H_local] o [H_local,512]
MP=1 storage: 64 + 64 + 64*512 = 32896 scalar values. MP=4 storage: 16 + 16 + 16*512 = 8224 scalar values.
State is updated after every tile and finally normalized.

ATTENTION.forward(x, start_pos)
Actual model-side producer/consumer boundary. Q path, KV path, Compressor, Indexer, cache and QCAU are wired below.

1. Q LOW-RANK PROJ
qr = q = q_norm(wq_a(x)) wq_a [1024,4096]
x [B,S,4096] -> qr [B,S,1024] qr is reused by Indexer.

2. Q HEAD EXPANSION
q = wq_b(qr) wq_b logical [H*Dh,1024] = [32768,1024]
global output [B,S,32768]. ColumnParallelLinear gives local [B,S,H_local*512].

3. Q RESHAPE + RoPE
unflatten(-1,[H_local,512]). q *= rsqrt(mean(q^2,last_dim)+eps). apply_rotary_emb(q[...,-64:], freqs_cis).
q [B,S,H_local,512] MP=1: H_local=64; MP=4: H_local=16.

4. KV LATENT PROJ
kv = kv_norm(wkv(x)) wkv [512,4096]
x [B,S,4096] -> kv [B,S,512]. apply_rotary_emb(kv[...,-64:], freqs_cis). Non-RoPE width=448.

5. KV QAT / ACTIVATION QUANT
act_quant(kv[...,:-64], block_size=64, inplace=True).
448 non-RoPE values = 7 blocks x 64. RoPE tail 64 stays in activation precision.
Output kv [B,S,512].

6. MAIN KV CACHE
self.kv_cache [B,N_cache,512]. ratio=0: N_cache=W=128. ratio=4: N_cache=128+1024=1152. ratio=128: N_cache=128+32=160.
Prefill: write current window. Decode: cache[:, start_pos % 128] = kv[:,0].

7. OPTIONAL MAIN COMPRESSOR
compressor(x,start_pos) when ratio != 0. wkv_c(x), wgate(x): [B,S,coff*512]. ratio=4: coff=2 overlap mode. score = wgate + ape. softmax over ratio positions. weighted sum -> compressed kv [B,S_c,512].
Writes compressed rows at cache offset W in decode mode.

8. OPTIONAL INDEXER, ratio=4
Inputs x [B,S,4096] and qr [B,S,1024]. index q [B,S,H_i_local,128], H_i=64 global; H_i_local=64/world_size (16 at MP=4). Indexer compressed KV [B,N_c,128]. index_score [B,S,N_c]. topk(min(512,N_c)) -> compressed_idx [B,S,K_c].
Future compressed positions become -1; legal positions receive offset.

9. WINDOW ADDRESS GENERATOR
get_window_topk_idxs(128,B,S,start_pos).
window_idx [B,S,128]. Future/unavailable addresses are -1. Decode p>=127 rotates circular order by p % 128.

10. TOP-K ADDRESS PACKET
ratio=0: topk_idxs = window_idx [B,S,128]. ratio!=0: cat(window_idx, compressed_idx) -> [B,S,K_total]. topk_idxs = int32.
Same address packet is reused for every local query head.

11. KV FEED TO QCAU
Prefill ratio=0: kv [B,S,512]. Prefill ratio!=0: if compressor emits, cat(current kv, compressed kv) [B,N,512]; otherwise current kv remains [B,S,512]. Decode: self.kv_cache[:B] [B,N_cache,512].
This is the exact kv argument passed to QCAU.

QCAU CORE INTERNAL WIRING: _sparse_attention_online()
One row below means one tile iteration. The loop repeats for tile_base = 0,64,128,...,K_total-1. This is the direct dataflow contract for an RTL QCAU attention engine.

Q INPUT BUFFER
q [B,S,H_local,Dh] Dh=512; H_local=64 MP=1 or 16 MP=4
q_float = q.float() Used for every tile of the same query row.

KV MEMORY
kv_float [B,N,512] N=128 window-only; ratio=4 decode N=1152; ratio=128 decode N=160. Each row is one latent K/V vector of width 512.

TOP-K ADDRESS MEMORY
topk_idxs [B,S,K_total] int32 tile_idxs = topk_idxs[...,tile_base:tile_base+64] tile_idxs [B,S,T], T=64 except final tile.

TILE CONTROLLER
tile_base = 0,64,128,... num_tiles = ceil(K_total/64).
Keeps m,l,o state for each [b,s,h] while changing the address slice. K_total=128 -> 2 tiles; K_total=512 -> 8 tiles.

1. VALIDITY + SAFE INDEX
valid = (idx >= 0) & (idx < N) Shape [B,S,T].
safe_idxs = clamp(idx,0,max(N-1,0)) Shape [B,S,T].
-1 and out-of-range values are safe for memory access but invalid for all math.

2. GATHER KV TILE
gather_index = safe_idxs.unsqueeze(-1).expand(B,S,T,Dh) shape [B,S,T,512].
torch.gather(kv_float, dim=1, index.reshape(B,S*T,512)) [B,S*T,512] -> reshape [B,S,T,512].
kv_tile = where(valid[...,None], kv_tile, 0).

3. QK DOT PRODUCT
scores = einsum('bshd,bstd->bsht', q_float, kv_tile)
q [B,S,H,512] kv_tile [B,S,T,512] scores [B,S,H,T].
For each b,s,h,t: dot = sum(d=0..511) q[b,s,h,d] * kv_tile[b,s,t,d].

4. SCALE + INVALID MASK
scores *= softmax_scale. Default scale = 512^(-1/2) = 0.04419417.
scores = where(valid.unsqueeze(2), scores, -inf)
masked scores [B,S,H,T].

RUNNING STATE REGISTER FILE
Initialized once per QCAU call: scores_max = -inf [B,S,H] sum_exp = 0 [B,S,H] acc_o = 0 [B,S,H,512]
All FP32 in reference. For one query b,s: m [H], l [H], o [H,512].

5. RUNNING MAX
tile_has_valid = valid.any(dim=-1).unsqueeze(-1) shape [B,S,1]. tile_max = scores.amax(dim=-1) [B,S,H]. candidate = maximum(scores_max_prev,tile_max). scores_max = where(tile_has_valid,candidate,scores_max_prev).
All-invalid tile leaves max unchanged.

6. OLD ACCUMULATOR RESCALE
old_scale = exp(scores_max_prev - scores_max). If tile_has_valid=False: old_scale=1.
This changes the exponent origin of old sum_exp and acc_o before adding this tile.
old_scale [B,S,H].

7. TILE EXPONENTIAL WEIGHTS
safe_scores_max = where(isfinite(scores_max),scores_max,0). probs = exp(scores - safe_scores_max[...,None]). probs = where(valid.unsqueeze(2),probs,0).
probs [B,S,H,T]. Invalid entries are exactly zero.

8. NORMALIZATION MASS UPDATE
sum_exp = sum_exp * old_scale + probs.sum(dim=-1).
sum_exp [B,S,H]. This is only real KV mass. Attention sink is added after all tiles.

9. WEIGHTED-V ACCUMULATION
acc_o = acc_o * old_scale.unsqueeze(-1) + einsum('bsht,bstd->bshd', probs, kv_tile).
probs [B,S,H,T] kv_tile [B,S,T,512] acc_o [B,S,H,512].
For each d: sum_t probs[h,t] * V[t,d].

10. TILE LOOP FEEDBACK
The new scores_max, sum_exp and acc_o become the previous state for tile_base += 64.
Loop count = ceil(K_total/64). No [B,S,H,K_total] probability matrix is stored.

11. ATTENTION SINK
sink = attn_sink.view(1,1,H)
If scores_max finite: exp(sink - scores_max). If scores_max=-inf and sink finite: 1. If both are -inf: 0.
Sink contributes to denominator only; no V vector.

12. FINAL DENOMINATOR + OUTPUT
sum_exp += sink_term. den = clamp_min(sum_exp,tiny_FP32). out = acc_o / den.unsqueeze(-1).
out [B,S,H_local,512]. Cast to q.dtype.
All-invalid row: acc_o=0, output=0 and remains finite.

OUTPUT TO Attention.forward()
o [B,S,H_local,512]
Next operations in model.py: inverse RoPE -> group view -> wo_a einsum -> wo_b row-parallel linear.

FUNCTIONAL CONTRACT FOR RTL
Required recurrence: m_new = max(m_old,tile_max) with invalid-tile no-op. l_new = l_old*exp(m_old-m_new) + sum(exp(score-m_new)). o_new = o_old*exp(m_old-m_new) + sum(exp(score-m_new)*V).
The physical PE count, SRAM banking and exp/reciprocal approximation are implementation choices; these dependencies and masks are not optional.
